description: The system is a collaborative project management platform built on Clean Architecture principles. The primary flow begins with Identity & Access Management and Infrastructure & Communication Services providing the security and connectivity foundation. Users interact through User & Access Control Adapters to manage their profiles and permissions. The core business logic is split between Project & Board Management, which handles the structural organization of work, and Team & Membership Management, which governs the collaborative relationships and roles within those projects. Data flows from external API requests through controllers and presenters into domain entities and repositories, with real-time updates propagated via Socket.IO.

components.name: Identity & Access Management
components.description: Manages user authentication, JWT token lifecycle, and real-time gateway connectivity for secure session handling.

components.name: Authentication & Real-time Delivery (Adapters & Config)
components.description: Acts as the entry point for the subsystem, handling HTTP requests for authentication and maintaining persistent WebSocket connections. It manages the JWT lifecycle (access/refresh tokens) and provides the necessary configuration for secure token generation and validation.

components.name: Role & Permission Management (Domain & Persistence)
components.description: Manages the definition and assignment of roles and permissions. This component encapsulates the business logic for RBAC, including the creation, retrieval, and deletion of roles, as well as the mapping of specific permissions to those roles within the persistence layer.

components.name: User Identity & Account Management (Domain & Persistence)
components.description: Handles the core user entity lifecycle, including registration, profile updates, and credential verification. It integrates password hashing services and enforces domain-specific constraints such as email uniqueness, account status (suspended/deactivated), and verification states.

components_relations.relation: Orchestrates identity verification and session lifecycle
components_relations.evidence: The AuthController and associated Use Cases (Login, Register, Verify) act as the primary consumer of the UserRepository and PasswordService.

components_relations.relation: Enforces access control policies on active sessions
components_relations.evidence: The RolesPermissionsGuard queries the RolePermissionRepository to resolve the effective permissions of the authenticated user's role.

components_relations.relation: Resolves authorization context for user entities
components_relations.evidence: The UserRepository interacts with the RoleRepository to validate role existence or to populate the user's domain model with associated role metadata.

components_relations.relation: Provides domain models for session configuration
components_relations.evidence: The persistence layer maps database records into domain entities used by AuthConfig and TokenService to embed role-based claims into JWT payloads.

components.name: Project & Board Domain
components.description: Orchestrates the core domain logic for projects and boards, including their creation, state management, and persistence.

components.name: Project Management & Orchestration
components.description: Acts as the primary entry point for project-related operations. It encompasses the REST adapters (controllers), application use cases for project lifecycle management (creation, deletion, retrieval), and the persistence implementation. It enforces project-specific business rules and domain exceptions.

components.name: Board Operations & Real-time Integration
components.description: Manages the functional logic of boards within projects, including state transitions and board-level use cases. Uniquely, it integrates the RealtimeService to ensure that board updates (like creation or deletion) are broadcasted immediately to connected clients via WebSockets.

components.name: Domain Entities & Response Presenters
components.description: Contains the core domain models and factories for both Projects and Boards, serving as the 'Enterprise Business Rules' layer. It also houses the Presenters responsible for transforming domain entities into specific data transfer formats for the UI, ensuring a decoupled view of the domain state.

components_relations.relation: Maps persistence models to domain entities and formats API responses
components_relations.evidence: The Project component acts as a consumer of the Domain layer. It uses ProjectFactory to instantiate entities from raw database data and utilizes ProjectPresenter to transform these entities into DTOs for HTTP responses.

components_relations.relation: Orchestrates board business logic and state transformations
components_relations.evidence: Board use cases consume domain entities to enforce business rules (e.g., checking board status) and use presenters to prepare data for both REST responses and WebSocket payloads.

components_relations.relation: Validates project existence for board-level operations
components_relations.evidence: Board use cases (Create/Delete) perform cross-component validation by calling the ProjectRepository to ensure a board is always associated with a valid, existing project.

components_relations.relation: Triggers cascading cleanup and real-time synchronization
components_relations.evidence: When a project is deleted, the system triggers a cascade to clean up associated boards and utilizes the RealtimeService to notify clients of the state change across the project scope.

components.name: Team & Membership Domain
components.description: Handles the domain logic for organizational structures, managing how users are grouped into teams and their specific memberships within projects.

components.name: Team Management Core
components.description: Responsible for the lifecycle and identity of organizational teams. It encapsulates the domain logic for creating, retrieving, and deleting teams, utilizing factories for entity instantiation and repositories for persistence.

components.name: Membership Lifecycle & Assignment
components.description: Manages the association between users and scopes (Teams or Projects). This component handles the creation of memberships and the assignment of roles, defining how a user is linked to a specific entity within the system.

components.name: Membership Query & Domain Validation
components.description: Provides complex query capabilities for retrieving membership details and enforces domain-specific constraints and exceptions. It handles the logic for listing members within teams or projects and ensures business rules (like preventing the removal of the last owner) are maintained.

components_relations.evidence: When a team is created, the core logic triggers the membership assignment use case to grant the creator "Owner" status, ensuring atomic setup of team identity and access.
During team removal, the core component relies on the membership repository to purge all associated user links, maintaining referential integrity at the domain level.
The lifecycle component acts as a coordinator that delegates state changes (Create/Update/Delete) to the repository implementation, which enforces domain rules like "last owner" protection.

The repository implementation uses mapping logic to transform raw database documents into rich Domain Entities defined in the Lifecycle component, ensuring the application layer works with valid domain objects.

components.name: Infrastructure & Communication Services
components.description: Provides low-level technical capabilities including database configurations (MongoDB/Redis), OTP generation, and external email client integration.

components.name: Configuration & External Clients
components.description: Manages the ingestion and validation of environment variables to configure core infrastructure services. It also provides the concrete implementation for external communication protocols, such as SMTP for email delivery.

components.name: OTP Management Service
components.description: A specialized domain-driven component handling the generation, persistence, and verification of One-Time Passwords. It encapsulates the business rules for OTP expiration, attempt limits, and secure validation.

components.name: Infrastructure Core & Exception Handling
components.description: Provides the central database connection management and a unified exception hierarchy. This component ensures that infrastructure-level errors (database timeouts, external service failures) are translated into a format the application can handle consistently.

components_relations.relation: Provides operational parameters and error definitions
components_relations.evidence: The configuration component supplies the necessary connection strings and environment-specific settings required for the database to initialize.

components_relations.relation: Consumes business policy and messaging protocols
components_relations.evidence: The OTP service relies on the configuration component to retrieve domain-specific constants and utilizes the concrete Email Client implementation.

components_relations.relation: Persists domain state and utilizes global error handling
components_relations.evidence: The OTP repositories interact with the Database component to manage the lifecycle of OTP entities.
The Database component calls into the Configuration component to resolve the MongoDB URI and connection options.

components.name: User & Access Control Adapters
components.description: Serves as the primary entry point for managing user profiles, roles, and granular permissions through REST controllers and presenters.

components.name: Permission & Board Access Adapters
components.description: Handles the external API surface for permission management and board-level access control. It transforms domain permission entities and role-permission mappings into structured API responses (Presenters) and coordinates the initial execution of permission-related use cases.

components.name: Identity & Role Management Adapters
components.description: Manages the primary entry points for User, Role, and Team resources. This component is responsible for orchestrating user profile updates, role definitions, and team assignments, ensuring that identity-related operations are correctly routed to the application layer.

components.name: Permission Domain Infrastructure
components.description: Provides the concrete implementation of permission-related domain logic, including the factory for creating permission objects, the repository for database persistence, and the specialized exception handling for access control violations.

components_relations.evidence: The controllers in the Adapters layer directly invoke use cases that rely on the Permission Domain Infrastructure for CRUD operations and domain object instantiation. Static analysis shows direct calls from execution paths to repository methods like create, findById, and update.

components_relations.relation: provides domain entities for API transformation
components_relations.evidence: The infrastructure layer instantiates and returns Domain Entities (Permission, RolePermission) which are consumed by the Adapters' Presenters to generate RESTful responses. This represents a data flow from the domain/persistence layer back to the external interface.

components_relations.relation: provides identity context for access control
components_relations.evidence: Identity adapters manage User and Role IDs which are required as input parameters for Board Access and Permission assignments. The RBAC configuration defined in the Identity component (Roles) directly constrains the valid operations within the Permission component.
